statement.summary: Theorem 9.1 is `detectWorstStatement`: for every schedule of the order-p subgroups, every family of traversal orders, both readings of a failing walk and every configuration, the read count returned by the Lean function `detect` is ≤ n^d · sopf_d(n). The 'algorithm' is modelled literally (`orbitWalk`, `compareTail`, `walkOrbit`, `subgroupTestAux`, `subgroupTest`, `detect`); the `O(·)` clause is not stated separately. `thmDetectWorstStatement` additionally bundles the correctness sentence that precedes the theorem (Lemma 3.4 restated, and correctness of `detect`).
deltas: N = n^d written out; sopf_d(n) = `sopfD n d = Σ_{p ∈ n.primeFactors} gaussBinom p d 1` (Common.lean).
The algorithm is a Lean function returning (verdict, reads); 'reads at most' is a bound on its second component.

The subgroup enumeration is an input `sched` (IsSchedule): every order-p cyclic subgroup (p | n prime) exactly once, in any order, with any generator. Computing it from representative lines is not modelled (no cell reads either way).
Traversal order: one per schedule entry, a duplicate-free list of all cells, fixed in advance (covers 'one shared order').
The orbit of u under ⟨w⟩ is walked as u, u+w, …, u+(p−1)w (order inside an orbit fixed by the generator; the paper leaves it open).
Both readings of a failing walk (stop at first mismatch / complete it) via `stopEarly : Bool`.
The O(sopf_d(n)·n^d) clause is the same quantity and is not frozen separately.
Standing hypotheses n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 2 explicit; alphabet Fin σ (the core bound `detect_reads_le_worst` holds for any alphabet).

\mathrm{sopf}_d(n)=\sum_{p\mid n}\gaussbinom d1_p

maps.label: standing hypotheses n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 2

tex.text: Fix integers $n\ge2$, $d\ge1$

maps.note: From Definition 2.1; not needed by the bound.

maps.label: the algorithm of §9 = `detect`

tex.text: \textbf{Algorithm.} For each prime $p\mid n$ and each of the $\gaussbinom d1_p$ order-$p$ cyclic subgroups $C=\langle\ww\rangle$ (enumerated via one representative line each, Lemma~\ref{lem:torsion}): traverse the cells in a fixed order (which may depend on the subgroup); for each yet-unvisited cell, walk its $C$-orbit ($p$ cells) checking equality; abort the subgroup at the first failing orbit. Report ``symmetric'' at the first subgroup all of whose orbits pass; report ``asymmetric'' if all subgroups fail.

lean.text:
| e :: rest =>
      let t := subgroupTest stopEarly s (ord e) e.1 e.2
      if t.1 then (true, t.2.2)
      else
        let r := detect stopEarly s ord rest
        (r.1, t.2.2 + r.2)

maps.note: `detect stopEarly s ord sched` runs the subgroup tests in schedule order and returns (verdict, total cells read). It is a Lean function, so the read count is computed, not postulated.

maps.label: for each prime p | n and each of the [d 1]_p order-p subgroups C = ⟨w⟩

tex.text: $p\mid n$ and each of the $\gaussbinom d1_p$ order-$p$ cyclic subgroups $C=\langle\ww\rangle$

lean.text: ∀ sched : List (ℕ × Lat n d), IsSchedule sched →

(∀ e ∈ sched, e.1.Prime ∧ e.1 ∣ n ∧ addOrderOf e.2 = e.1) ∧
  (sched.map fun e => AddSubgroup.zmultiples e.2).Nodup ∧
  ∀ C : AddSubgroup (Lat n d), IsPrimeOrderCyclic C →
    ∃ e ∈ sched, AddSubgroup.zmultiples e.2 = C

maps.note: The subgroups are an INPUT list of pairs (p, w), each order-p cyclic subgroup (p | n prime) generated by exactly one entry. Statements quantify over all such lists: any order (primes may even interleave — the paper's nesting is a special case) and any generator w of each subgroup.

maps.label: enumerated via one representative line each (Lemma 3.3)

tex.text: enumerated via one representative line each

lean.text: addOrderOf e.2 = e.1

maps.note: Not modelled as a computation: the schedule is assumed given, with a generator of order p per subgroup. Every such generator is (n/p)·y for a representative y of the line, so the choice of 'representative line' is covered; producing the list costs no cell reads in either model.

maps.label: prime factorization of n given

tex.text: Assume the prime factorization of $n$ is given

lean.text: e.1.Prime ∧ e.1 ∣ n

maps.note: The primes p | n enter only through the schedule; no factorization cost is modelled (the paper also counts only cell reads).

maps.label: traverse the cells in a fixed order (may depend on the subgroup)

tex.text: traverse the cells in a fixed order (which may depend on the subgroup)

lean.text: ∀ ord : ℕ × Lat n d → List (Lat n d), (∀ e ∈ sched, IsTraversalOrder (ord e)) →
ord.Nodup ∧ ∀ u : Lat n d, u ∈ ord

maps.note: One order per schedule entry, each listing every cell exactly once and fixed in advance (independent of the configuration); one shared order is the special case `fun _ => o`.

maps.label: for each yet-unvisited cell, walk its C-orbit (p cells)

tex.text: for each yet-unvisited cell, walk its $C$-orbit ($p$ cells) checking equality

lean.text: if u ∈ visited then subgroupTestAux stopEarly s p w us visited
(List.range p).map fun k => u + k • w

maps.note: Visited cells are skipped at no cost; the orbit is walked as u, u+w, …, u+(p−1)w. The paper does not fix the order inside an orbit; Lean fixes it to powers of the chosen generator w (with w ranging over all generators). This only affects early-stop read counts, and all bounds hold for it.

maps.label: visited = cells of orbits already walked in this subgroup

tex.text: yet-unvisited cell

lean.text: let t := subgroupTestAux stopEarly s p w us (visited ++ cells)
subgroupTestAux stopEarly s p w ord []

maps.note: The visited set starts empty for every subgroup and grows by each passed orbit; the failing orbit is not marked (the subgroup is aborted anyway).

maps.label: abort the subgroup at the first failing orbit

tex.text: abort the subgroup at the first failing orbit

lean.text: else (false, 1, r.2)

maps.note: A failing orbit ends the subgroup's traversal; it counts as one visited orbit and its reads are charged.

maps.label: report symmetric at the first passing subgroup; asymmetric if all fail

tex.text: Report ``symmetric'' at the first subgroup all of whose orbits pass; report ``asymmetric'' if all subgroups fail

lean.text: if t.1 then (true, t.2.2)

maps.note: `true` = 'symmetric'. The reads of all processed subgroups are added; later subgroups are not run.

maps.label: one read per visited cell; anchor cached

tex.text: we charge one read per visited cell: the first cell of an orbit walk (the \emph{anchor}) is read once and its value cached, and each subsequent cell of the orbit is read once and compared to the cached value

lean.text:
| a :: rest =>
      let r := compareTail stopEarly s (s a) rest
      (r.1, r.2 + 1)

if s x = a then
        let r := compareTail stopEarly s a xs
        (r.1, r.2 + 1)

maps.note: The anchor costs 1 and its value `s a` is passed on; each compared cell costs 1.

maps.label: a failing walk may stop at the first mismatch or be completed

tex.text: A failing orbit walk may stop at its first mismatch or be completed

lean.text: else if stopEarly then (false, 1)
∀ (stopEarly : Bool)

maps.note: Both variants are one Boolean parameter; every statement here is quantified over it.

maps.label: correctness sentence (Lemma 3.4)

tex.text: a configuration is shift-symmetric iff it is fixed by some order-$p$ cyclic subgroup with $p\mid n$

lean.text:
(IsShiftSymmetric s ↔
      ∃ C : AddSubgroup (Lat n d), IsPrimeOrderCyclic C ∧ s ∈ fixedBy (Fin σ) C)
∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ p ∣ n ∧ IsAddCyclic C ∧ Nat.card C = p

maps.note: Prose before the theorem, bundled into `thmDetectWorstStatement`; not part of the theorem environment.

maps.label: the algorithm is correct

tex.text: Correctness is

lean.text: ((detect stopEarly s ord sched).1 = true ↔ IsShiftSymmetric s)

maps.note: The paper attributes correctness to Lemma 3.4; Lean states and proves correctness of `detect` itself (all schedules, orders, readings). Bundled into the whole statement, so the Lean whole is stronger than Theorem 9.1 alone.
